thread:
olivia: FYI I sketched an approach for an 'activation window' for atomic bundle activations in airgapped on‑prem upgrades. Want to align on fallback/playbook and agent semantics before I formalize an RFC.

arjun: brief summary pls — what do you mean by activation window? :eyes:

olivia: high level: bundle apply has two phases — transfer+verify, then activation. The activation marker is a short TTL lease that signals "go live" for all components. If activation fails or is partial, we have an automatic fallback path that reverts to previous image.

maya: curious — is the lease coordinated through the control-plane sidecar or purely agent-driven?

olivia: agent-driven with an operator-signed activation blob. Sequence: 1) seed transfer, 2) verify signatures + hashes, 3) stage files (no swap), 4) write activation blob (signed, timestamped, TTL), 5) agents perform atomic switch on activation.

ben: note: for airgapped environments we can't rely on central time syncing. We should use monotonic counters and activation epochs in addition to wall time TTL. That avoids clock drift problems.

sasha: security: activation blob must include key id, bundle digest, operator identity, and a nonce. Replay protection is critical. Also, if operators revoke a bundle, we need a revocation marker tied to the same epoch.

olivia: agreed. I propose activation blob fields like: 
```
{
  epoch: 42,
  bundle_digest: "sha256:..",
  operator_sig: "sig..",
  nonce: "random32",
  valid_from: 1680000000,
  ttl_seconds: 86400
}
```
agents should accept activation iff epoch > current_epoch OR (epoch == current_epoch and signature valid).

arjun: how do we handle partial topologies? e.g., some nodes activate, others don't (network partition). Does the fallback auto-run?

olivia: fallback rules: if < N% of nodes report activation success within window W, automatically initiate staged rollback on the subset that switched. Also issue operator alert. The playbook recommends conservative defaults: N=80, W=15m.

maya: do we support canary groups? Could activation blob target groups by tag so we can roll gradually?

olivia: yes, activation blob can include target selectors (tags or roles). Agents ignore blob if selector doesn't match. This keeps the activation semantics consistent across canary and full rollouts.

ben: implementation detail: make agent apply idempotent — write staged files under "/var/lib/redwood/staged/<bundle_epoch>" and the activation step simply symlink swap or atomic rename. That makes rollbacks trivial: remove symlink and restart.

olivia: exactly. Also include a small safety: before activation, agents verify disk space + health hooks. If a node fails healthhooks, it never activates and signals back.

sasha: what about offline revocation? If operator decides to revoke after activation window expires, we need a revocation blob that agents fetch via out-of-band seed or operator poke. The agent must prefer revocation over activation even if TTL still valid.

olivia: good call. We'll add revocation blob with higher precedence and a revocation-epoch. Agents will apply revocation immediately, try to restore previous state, and keep a lock so operator can inspect.

deploy-bot: CI check: activation blob schema validated and unit tests for agent epoch logic present in PR #4271 :white_check_mark:

arjun: how do we avoid split-brain where two different activation blobs for different bundles have same epoch? Need a deterministic tie-breaker (bundle_digest compare).

ben: tie-breaker: lexicographic compare of bundle_digest plus operator priority. Document it but prefer avoiding same epoch reuse in operator tooling.

maya: playbook suggestion (short):
1) Operator stage bundle -> transfer completed :white_check_mark:
2) Operator sign activation blob with epoch, tags, TTL -> publish to control plane or local seed :white_check_mark:
3) Wait for N% ACK within W -> if yes, mark rollout complete :tada:, else trigger automatic rollback on activated nodes and escalate to oncall :rotating_light:
4) If revocation issued after completion, follow revocation procedure and schedule a repair.

olivia: I'll add these to the RFC draft. Open question: default TTL — 24h? shorter makes rollbacks faster but complicates slow networks. Thoughts?

sasha: default 24h is fine but require operator to be explicit for >72h. Also add an audit trail entry on every activation/rollback with operator id and signature.

arjun: make TTL configurable per-target group. Some isolated sites will need longer windows.

ben: ops: add a manual "force-commit" operator action that upgrades activation state to permanent (clears revocation path) after manual verification. That avoids accidental rollbacks long-term. Log it.

olivia: perfect. I'll incorporate all this and push an RFC update tonight. Will include sequence diagrams and agent state machine (+ pseudocode). Thanks all. :heart:

maya: :+1: ping me if you want help with agent tests.

sasha: I'll write the security checklist for the RFC (signing, replay, revocation).

arjun: small nit — include a compatibility shim for older agents that only understand "activation_marker" without epoch. We'll reject and require a staged migration.

olivia: noted. RFC will include migration path. Closing for now, opening PR later.

deploy-bot: RFC link created: https://go/redwood/rfc/airgap-activation-window-2186 (draft)
